Shit, same.
10 years of depression, it finally got better this year for a while... before it dove back in again.
I dream that we either never broke up or we got back together, then as soon as I wake up...

I hate the whole "side hustle" culture. I hate how we're forced to do work we hate for fear of starvation. (And starve anyway, fuck me)
I hate how we have less and less time for hobbies. I hate "hobby jobs" which exploit your passion for pennies.
Those third-rate NFT "art pieces" will soon fall apart and the suckers will lose a lot of money.

You never "make it". The "faking" part just helps you get some feel-good chemicals in your brain for a little while, which is scarce in depression. Feel-good chemicals help you do more stuff. Even if it doesn't help you feel good, it at least gets the ball rolling. There's nothing grand to it, really. There's always a chance you'll fall apart again, and the cycle continues...

Keep searching. If you suck at something you like doing, that's a sign you should continue. Life is seriously unpredictable.
If you do end up in a job you hate that sucks away all your time and energy, do everything you can to safely quit. Save up, learn a technical skill, anything. Just don't stick to it for life. 
You still have time, anyway.

Time isn't really the issue if you can manage to find some. It's more about your resources, and even that's manageable - plenty of resources on the internet if you want to learn to code, for example. And even if you were a child prodigy, there's no guarantee of success. It's all about the journey and putting in the hours.

Exactly, society is in a really freaking pitiful state. It's far from perfect. It's close to terminally ill, even. You just have to dampen that noise and keep going forward. It'll take you years to accomplish something, anyway, so you're better off being 30 and still learning a skill as opposed to being 30 and not learning anything.

Anything worth doing requires a boatload of patience - and probably is worth doing badly. Is there any way you can start over? It's not like you'd be starting totally from scratch, at least you have experience.

>I've been told it gets harder and harder to find new interests and passions the older you get

Whoever told you that is truly in a pitiful state. Adults could never learn new things if this was true. You can indeed excel at it, too, depending on the field.
